correctness.rationale: A fixed finite set of labels has exact hypergeometric selection-pattern probabilities (d_n)_s(n-d_n)_u/(n)_{s+u}, giving a uniform relative O_R(log n/n) error against independent geometric discovery times over the O(log n) relevant rounds. Mixed factorial moments converge to independent Poisson first-appearance counts. Exact unseen-count factorial moments and two-sided completion-time tightness justify the infinite offset sum and the joint terminal location/multiplicity law. Absolutely convergent phase sums admit Mellin Fourier unfolding; Gamma has no zeros; logarithmic equidistribution yields the log-series weights. The finite-state inclusion-exclusion checker reports 365 passed assertions, but infinite claims rest on the analytic arguments in RESULT.md.

value.rationale: The terminal batch size is a natural output statistic of macroscopic group coupon sampling: unlike singleton draws, more than one coupon can be discovered in the completion round. The theorem solves its entire fixed-multiplicity phase family and the exact meaningful logarithmic averaging law, showing nonconvergence even while the averaged law is a familiar, normalized log-series distribution. The derived unique-terminal-type probability is a direct operational invariant and is not determined by the expected completion time or a one-time deficit approximation alone.
